name: bootgpt
works_with: QEMU, or a real BIOS PC; built on macOS with Homebrew
short: A tiny language model that runs from a PC's boot sector with no OS and dreams up a fake Linux boot log.
what: The boot record is 512 bytes of hand-written assembly. It loads an 11.5 KB int8 model from the next 23 sectors and runs it in 16-bit real mode on a 386, with no OS or C runtime. The model is a small character-level network trained only to write a believable Linux boot log, with made-up timestamps and hardware. The Python training script simulates the exact integer math, so its output matches the boot sector character for character.
who: People who enjoy boot sector tricks, assembly and tiny neural networks. There is nothing practical to use beyond the demo.
needs: nasm and qemu (the README installs them with Homebrew)
Optional: a USB stick and a BIOS PC to boot it for real

steps.title: Build and run it
steps.text: `build.sh` builds the image and `run.sh` boots it in QEMU. Any keypress reboots the machine.
steps.code:
brew install nasm qemu
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install numpy
./build.sh
./run.sh

steps.title: Boot real hardware (optional)
steps.text: `disk.img` is a normal boot image. The README says you can write it to a USB stick with dd and boot any BIOS machine. It only reads its own sectors.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `./run.sh` and watch it print lines like `[  1.883084] NET: Registered protocol family 16`, mixed with half-garbled PCI and ACPI messages for hardware that never existed.

watch: The README gives no exact dd command. Only try the USB route if you know how to write an image to the right device.
The README does not name a licence.
The install line uses Homebrew. On other systems you need to get nasm and qemu yourself.
